admin.tip: This tab is read-only: the operator controls are inert. Paste the admin key to unlock them — it stays in this tab only (sessionStorage), is sent as a Bearer header and never appears in the URL.
admin.tip_admin: This tab is in admin mode. The key lives in sessionStorage for this tab only; signing out clears it.
admin.rejected: key rejected — check it against auth.admin_key in config.yaml
app.snap_src: Live pull from /healthz and /stats, patched in the background every 2 s — no reload, no lost scroll position. Every number carries an explanation: hover it.
app.tagline: Router Inference Policy Proxy for LLM Engines — Fleet overview
app.title: RIPPLE — Fleet overview
banner.no_guard: Eviction guard OFF: at least one backend delivers no residency or capacity signals (FA-18 inactive).
banner.no_identity: Identity OFF: the address counts as the identity (RB-9 violated).
calib.confirm: Calibrate {node}? This loads models on the node and may evict others.{what}{risk} The node must hold no active thread. Currently: {now}.
calib.fit: fit slope {slope} s/GB · intercept {intercept} s · worst {worst} s/GB · linearity {linearity}
calib.negative_intercept: the intercept is negative: the fit subtracts a fixed load time. Shown as measured — not rounded away.
dist.empty: no threads bound and no requests — the distribution has nothing to show yet.
dist.note_many: Actual share measured over the bound thread slots, not over requests.
dist.note_noslot: Without a bound slot there is no actual share: the share would be 0 divided by 0. The requests above are therefore the only reliable value for this block.
dist.note_one: With one bound slot the actual share is necessarily 0 or 100 % — the deviation here is not a fault of the distribution but the resolution of the sample.
dist.req_window_tip: Requests RIPPLE sent to this node for this model inside the window — a model without a warm thread still shows its traffic here.
dist.requests_tip: Requests per node — requests RIPPLE has sent to this node since the start, and their share of all requests. Not to be confused with the thread share above: requests and slots are two different currencies.
fleet.cal_busy: a calibration is running on this node
fleet.cal_held: the node holds an active thread (force=1 overrides this, at the cost of that conversation's prefix cache)
fleet.cal_locked: {models} is locked and resident here — a calibration would take its memory. Unlock it first; force does not override this.
fleet.cal_ready: measure this node's load time — no thread bound, no locked model in the way
fleet.source_tip: config.yaml is the hand-written baseline. A node added at the page lives in the overlay ~/.ripple/fleet.yaml and can be removed again; a node from config.yaml can only be disabled.
foot.readonly: read-only: the page writes nothing except calibration, maintenance window, model policy and replication
foot.source: no CDN, no framework, no build step
key.help: Admin key required — set it on the key page (/keys). It stays in this tab.
lang.label: Language
legend.note: Colour never carries the message alone: every state has its own shape and fill — filled circle, half circle, filled triangle, open square, droplet, cross, hollow triangle. That stays readable in greyscale and with red-green colour blindness.
load.reset_tip: Zero the ledger and start again from now.
lock.builtin_tip: {model} is an oMLX builtin — resident without weights, routed to by nothing: always locked, never releasable. No request is sent to it.
lock.confirm_lock:
Lock model "{model}"?

While it is loaded, RIPPLE refuses every request that would need its memory (503 model_locked) — on every node that holds it. The model stays in /v1/models and keeps being served; nothing changes on oMLX, the lock survives a restart of RIPPLE.
lock.confirm_unlock:
Release the lock on "{model}"?

RIPPLE may then evict the model again when another request needs the memory.
lock.may_evict: · RIPPLE may evict the model when a request needs the memory
lock.no_key: · cannot be changed without the admin key: {help}
lock.nowhere: · not loaded anywhere right now — the lock refuses nothing
lock.warn_saved: {model}: lock saved, but it cannot be resident anywhere right now — {reason}
lock.warn_tip: The lock is stored, but it cannot be resident anywhere right now. On {host}: {reason}. Nothing is evicted for it — unlock what blocks it, or lock the model on a node where it fits.
log.filter_hint: filters the rows below, not the buffer
maint.clear_confirm: End maintenance for {node}? The node returns to the pool.
maint.cleared: {node}: maintenance ended, back in the pool.
maint.confirm:
Set maintenance for {node}: {span}?

The node accepts no new work, running requests finish. Nothing changes on oMLX itself.
maint.end_tip: end the window — the node returns to the pool
maint.label: Maintenance
models.dim_tip: available but not loaded — a click expands the rows
models.nr_dispatch: not dispatched here — this node does not offer the model, so no request can reach it
models.nr_resident: listed but not loaded here — the first request would pay a cold load
models.routable: routable here — RIPPLE dispatches this model to this node
models.tps_cap_none: no calibrated capability for this node in config.yaml
models.tps_measured: measured {v} tok/s on this node since the service started
models.tps_never: not measured yet: no request for this model has finished on this node since the service started — a measured zero would be shown as 0.0, not as a dash
nodes.api_key_hint: The key this node's own oMLX accepts on /v1/models. A node inherits nothing from defaults: leave it empty for a read-only node — it joins the fleet, but its model list stays unreadable and placement cannot pick it by name.
nodes.added_readonly: {name} added read-only — no key, so its model list could not be read ({detail}).
nodes.repl_key_note: Replication to this node uses a second, separate value: its oMLX admin key, hosts[].replication.api_key in config.yaml.
nodes.confirm:
Add {name} ({address}) to the fleet?
weight {weight} · site {site} · role {role}
nodes.disabled: {name} is disabled and stays in the fleet — enable it with one call when it is back.
nodes.drain_note: No new work goes to this node from now on; running requests finish. If the deadline passes, nothing is removed and the node stays disabled.
nodes.drain_wait: waits up to {v} s for them
nodes.err.admin: The admin key was refused — this tab still holds the previous one. Enter the current one from `config.yaml` (`auth.admin_key`) in the admin field; it is stored in this tab again.
nodes.err.models: The node answered; its model list could not be read ({detail}).
nodes.err.node_id: Something answered, but not this node ({detail}).
nodes.name: Name
nodes.need_address: An address is needed first, e.g. http://192.0.2.40:8000.
nodes.need_cidr: A network is needed first, e.g. 192.0.2.0/24.
nodes.remove_config: declared in config.yaml — disable it instead
nodes.removed: {name} removed after {v} s, {n} thread slot(s) released.
panel.calib.idle: nothing started yet — press "Calibrate" on a node card.
panel.maint.idle: nothing set yet — press "Maintenance" on a node card.
panel.policy.idle: nothing changed yet — pick the state in the node column of the model table.
panel.repl.idle: nothing checked yet — pick source, model and target, then "Check".
params.flap: {n} failed probes until a node counts as down
params.rebind_on: on · max {n}/h · gain ≥ {gain}× prefill · cooldown {cooldown} s
params.unhealthy_after: {n} failed probes — no longer the effective threshold, see placement flap_guard_failures
phase.load: loading (load) — the weights are not in memory yet, the request waits

policy.confirm_hide:
Hide model "{model}" on {node}?

It disappears from /v1/models once every node hides it — Hermes and opencode then lose it from their list. RIPPLE no longer routes it here, nothing changes on oMLX.
policy.confirm_restore:
Put model "{model}" on {node} back in service?

It appears in /v1/models again as soon as a node offers it, and RIPPLE routes it here again.
policy.head: Rules without a row in the model table
policy.intro: The node no longer offers these models, the rule is in the model file all the same. in service takes it back.
policy.no_key: Rules without a row in the model table need the admin key — set it on the key page (/keys), then the page reads them when Operations is opened.
policy.none: no rule without a row — every rule in {file} belongs to a model its node offers.
policy.orphan_since_tip: When the operator set the rule, local time of the machine RIPPLE runs on.
policy.orphan_why: The node no longer offers this model, but the rule is in {file} — that is why it has no row in the model table. It would take the model out of routing again the moment it is offered.
policy.read_failed: rules without a row not read: {nodes} — this node's admin view does not answer.
policy.unread: Rules without a row in the model table are read when Operations is opened.
reason.budget: The fleet's hourly move budget is spent.
reason.conflict: No node could take the request without evicting a running thread.
reason.cooldown: The thread moved just recently; a move back inside the cooldown is priced higher.
reason.cost_exceeds_ttl: The prefill would take longer than the thread's slot has left.
reason.degraded_host: The preferred node was degraded; the request went to the healthy one.
reason.ephemeral: One-off request without a thread: no slot, no cache, only load decides.
reason.fallback: The first node failed; the request was retried on the other one.
reason.gain_below_band: The gain stays under the cost times the safety factor plus the measured noise band.
reason.model_list_unavailable: The node's model list could not be read — whether it carries the model is unknown. Check the node's admin key.
reason.model_pinned: The model is pinned on this node and must not be evicted.
reason.moved: The thread was moved: the prefill pays for itself over the turns that remain.
reason.new_thread: New thread; the node was chosen by current load and residency.
reason.no_candidate: No further node left for a retry.
reason.no_healthy_host: No healthy node offers this model.
reason.no_repayment: The prefill would cost more than the remaining turns save.
reason.one_shot: Request that deliberately holds no thread — slots and slot eviction do not apply to it.
reason.pinned: This conversation has spent its moves inside the window.
reason.rebind: The thread was moved to this node to smooth the distribution.
reason.slot_evict: All slots were held by idle threads — the oldest gave up its place.
reason.thread: This conversation already has a thread on this node — the prefix cache stays valid, nothing is reloaded.
repl.cancel_confirm: Cancel the copy to {dst}? Nothing is registered; the copy started so far stays.
repl.cancel_note: nothing is registered; the copy stays and is resumed on the next run.
repl.cancelled: cancel requested — the job stops after the running rsync block.
repl.confirm: Copy model {model} from {src} to {dst}? {size} GB, {free} GB free. {dst} leaves the pool for the duration; the reload unloads every model there.
repl.free_tip: Free space on the file system of the target model directory, read with df over SSH. The pre-check requires size × replication.free_space_factor (default 1.05).
repl.model_tip: Model on the source node — only models this node offers.
repl.overwrite_tip: Replace an existing model on the target. Without the tick the pre-check refuses if the model is already there — better to refuse than to copy half.
repl.path_tip: Target path: the target node's first configured model_root plus the model's relative sub-path. The copy lands in .replication-incoming/ first and is renamed afterwards.
repl.progress_tip: Progress from the rsync progress line the run actually used: --info=progress2 on GNU rsync, --progress on openrsync (macOS), and no line at all when neither is accepted. The job records the flag it got.
repl.report_tip: Report of the job: bytes moved, duration and rate.
repl.settings_tip: The source's parameters were written flat onto the target (without display_name, description, active_profile_name — the PUT does not take those) and read back afterwards. Every deviation is listed here and turns the job red.
repl.size_tip: Estimated size of the model directory on the source node (actual_size, else estimated_size).
repl.source_tip: Source node — the files are read from here and its parameters are taken over.
repl.target_tip: Target node — it leaves the pool for the duration of the job, because the reload unloads every model there.
restart.accepted: accepted — the process ends in about {v} s and launchd starts it again. The page waits for the service and reconnects by itself.
restart.back: the service answers again: build {commit}, up {n} s — the page reconnected by itself.
restart.confirm:
Restart RIPPLE?

The process ends and launchd starts it again about {v} s later. Requests that are still in flight are cut, thread bindings are lost and rebuilt on the first contact, and this page reconnects by itself — the footer then shows the new build.commit. The operator's own session runs through this service: the request that is streaming at that moment ends with the process.{busy}
restart.confirm_busy: Right now {n} request(s) are in flight on {hosts} — cancelling this question leaves them running, a restart cuts them off.
restart.delay: the process ends {v} s after the answer
restart.force_confirm:
Restart anyway?

{n} request(s) are still in flight on {hosts} — the one that is streaming right now is the session this page was opened from, and it ends with the process. The service answered: {msg}
restart.gone: the service has not answered for {n} s — nothing listens on this port any more. The launchd job is the place to look.
restart.not_supervised: Not started by launchd, so nothing would start it again — the service refuses to end itself:
restart.pending: a restart is on its way
restart.rate_limited: 429 — the admin limiter refused the call, try again in a moment: {msg}
restart.reason.inflight: {n} request(s) are still in flight on {hosts} — the one that is streaming right now ends with the process.
restart.reason.inherited_label: RIPPLE carries the launchd label `{label}`, but it inherited it from another job: its parent is not launchd (ppid {ppid}, not 1), so nothing would start it again after it ended — it refuses to end itself. Start it as the launchd job `ai.ripple` to use this control.
restart.reason.label_not_owner: RIPPLE carries the launchd label `{label}`, but that job does not own this process: `launchctl print` does not name pid {pid}. Nothing would start it again after it ended, so it refuses to end itself. Start it as the launchd job `ai.ripple` to use this control.
restart.reason.no_label: RIPPLE has no launchd label (XPC_SERVICE_NAME is unset or `0`), so nothing would start it again after it ended — it refuses to end itself. Start it as the launchd job `ai.ripple` to use this control.
restart.reason.query_failed: RIPPLE carries the launchd label `{label}`, but launchd did not answer the ownership query (`launchctl print` failed or is not installed), so it is unproven that this job would start the process again — it refuses to end itself. Start it as the launchd job `ai.ripple` to use this control.
sec.calib.body: Measures how long this node needs to load its own models and stores the rate, so the cold-start estimate comes from the node instead of a constant. The node must hold no active thread: calibration loads models and can evict others.
sec.calib.hint: operator action per node, admin key required
sec.dist.hint: target against actual share of the thread slots
sec.fleet.hint: one node per card: state, address, memory against the ceiling, load
sec.load.hint: idle, prefill and decode per node, sampled every 10 s
sec.log.hint: ring buffer of the last 200 — why a request landed on this node
sec.maint.body: A maintenance window is routing state, not a second control plane for oMLX: the node accepts no new work, running requests finish, a bound thread falls over to the other node. Only when the card says drained is the machine free for an update — at draining (n) wait, do nothing else. The window lives in the maintenance file (placement.maintenance_file, default ~/.ripple/maintenance.yaml) and survives a restart; with minutes it ends by itself, without it runs until someone ends it. It is set and ended on the node card.
sec.maint.hint: take a node out of service gently, admin key required
sec.models.hint: one row per (model, node); models that are not loaded are dimmed
sec.nodes.add.body: The address is what you would type in a browser: http://host:port. The scheme may be left out.
sec.nodes.add.hint: One address, one preview, one confirmation.
sec.nodes.body: A node is read first and written second: the preview asks the machine through RIPPLE (POST /admin/nodes?dry_run=true), shows what it answered and writes nothing. Only the confirmation changes the fleet, and what it changes lives in the runtime overlay — config.yaml stays the hand-written baseline.
sec.nodes.hint: The machines that serve the fleet — add one here, take one out with a drain.
sec.nodes.remove.body: A node declared in config.yaml cannot be removed at runtime — the file is the baseline. Disable it instead.
sec.nodes.remove.hint: A drain, not a cut: no new work, the running requests finish.
sec.nodes.scan.body: Every address in the range is asked for its identity on the port given. A sweep is traffic on the network: it runs only when you press the button, and only with the admin key.
sec.nodes.scan.hint: The sweep of ripple discover --scan, over a CIDR.
sec.ops.hint: maintenance, models, calibration and parameters — operator actions and reference, not part of the overview
sec.params.body: Values as they apply after defaults, ${VAR} expansion and validation. Routing policy — weights, spill thresholds, thread lifetimes, rebind bounds, balance hysteresis — is set at the page and survives a restart: ~/.ripple/fleet.yaml is an overlay over config.yaml, which stays the baseline. Identity, transport and limits cannot be set here; they are shown with the reason instead of an input.
sec.params.hint: routing policy is set here and survives a restart; identity, transport and limits are not
sec.policy.body: Two levels, both pure RIPPLE state — nothing is loaded, unloaded or changed on oMLX. disabled: RIPPLE sends no more requests for this model to this node; the model stays in /v1/models as long as another node offers it. hidden: the model disappears from /v1/models once every node hides it — Hermes and opencode lose it from their list, which is why the page asks first. in service takes the state back. It is set in the model table, column node; it lives in the model file (placement.model_policy_file, default ~/.ripple/models.yaml) and survives a restart.
sec.policy.body2: The table comes from /healthz and only knows models a node offers right now. A rule for a model the node no longer offers would have no row there — it would live only in the model file and would take the model out of routing again the moment it is offered. Such rules without a row are therefore listed below with the same in service; they are read when this block is opened, with the admin key.
sec.policy.hint: take a model on a node out of routing or hide it, including a rule without a row, admin key required
sec.repl.body: A model is placed on the target node as files, registered there with reload and given the source's parameters. One model at a time, only on explicit instruction. The target leaves the pool for the duration — reload unloads every model there —, running requests finish, a bound thread falls over to the other node. Before the start this block says what is copied, how large it is and how much space is free; an interrupted copy is resumed, not restarted. Runbook: docs/replication.md.
sec.repl.hint: copy one model from one node to the other, admin key required
sec.restart.body: The one control that ends the process it runs in. The process ends, launchd starts it again about a second later. Requests that are still in flight are cut, thread bindings are lost and rebuilt on the first contact, and this page reconnects by itself — the footer then shows the new build.commit. The operator's own session runs through this service: the request that is streaming at that moment ends with the process. That is why a restart with requests in flight needs a second confirmation. Whether the process may end itself at all is launchd's answer, not the page's (/healthz → restart); without the admin key the control stays off and says why.
sec.restart.hint: end the process and let launchd start it again, admin key required
state.degraded: answers, but over threshold or with errors
state.loading: is loading a model, accepts work
state.maintenance: taken out of the pool by the operator
threads.delete_confirm: Delete this thread? Its prefix cache is gone for good.
threads.silent_tip: silent — no request for this thread in over {min} min. It keeps its slot and its row until the TTL expires, and only the same conversation can wake it. The thread count is read as "what is running", so the row says when that is no longer true.
tip.addr_sw: Address switches — How often RIPPLE has fallen back to another address of the same node since the start.
tip.address: Address — Address RIPPLE currently uses for the node; the alternatives serve the site switch (FA-21).
tip.ceiling: Ceiling — Upper bound the guard checks against; nothing is loaded beyond it.
tip.cache: Prefix cache — tokens of the last answer on this node that the server took from its own prefix cache, against that request's prompt. 0 means the prefix was cold; a dash means the server reported nothing.
tip.ctx: Context — Maximum context length of the model in tokens.
tip.d_bar: Duration bar — Length relative to the longest decision in the buffer — shows outliers, not absolute values.
tip.d_count: Entries — How many decisions the ring buffer currently holds (200 at most).
tip.d_dur: Duration — Time from acceptance to the last response line, in milliseconds.
tip.d_host: Node — Node the request went to.
tip.d_med: Median / p90 — Median and 90th percentile of the duration over all entries in the buffer.
tip.d_prompt: Prompt size — Characters in the request's prompt; determines the prefill effort.
tip.d_reason: Reason — Why this node — the explanation is on the chip.
tip.d_status: Status — HTTP status the client received.
tip.d_time: Time — Moment of the decision, local time of the machine RIPPLE runs on.
tip.delta: Deviation — Actual minus target in percentage points.
tip.errors: Errors — Failed requests to this node since the start.
tip.guard: Memory guard — Whether the node refuses a load that would push memory over the hard limit — HTTP 507 instead of eviction.
tip.hard: hard limit — Share of the ceiling from which the guard refuses a load. Dashed in the bar. The guard computes with the estimate (used_bytes), not with the measurement — the dashed line therefore applies to the hatched estimate stretch, not to the full fill.
tip.headroom: Headroom — ceiling minus measured used memory: how much room is left before the guard steps in.
tip.inflight: inflight — Requests running on this node at this moment.
tip.k_5xx: 503 / 507 — 503 = no node could take the request; 507 = a node refused the load for memory reasons.
tip.k_err: Errors — Requests that ended in an error.
tip.k_hits: Thread hits — Requests that hit an existing thread and reused its prefix cache.
tip.k_new: Threads new / evicted — Newly created threads and threads that had to make room for a new one.
tip.k_rebind: Rebind — Threads moved to the other node to smooth the distribution.
tip.k_req: Requests total — All requests since the service started.
tip.k_uptime: Uptime — Runtime of the RIPPLE process since the last start.
tip.load_completion_tokens: completion tokens — Sum of usage.completion_tokens over all answers, as the node counted them.
tip.load_cross: Cross-check — The nodes' own count from their SQLite (range=today), shown beside RIPPLE's ledger and never added to it. The gap between the two is the traffic that went past RIPPLE.
tip.load_decode: decode — Exclusive time this node spent generating tokens. The second line is its share of the sampled window.
tip.load_decode_s: decode seconds — Sum of usage.generation_duration over all answers, measured by oMLX itself. Not the client's wait.
tip.load_hide_idle: Hide idle — the percentages then refer to the time under load only (window minus idle), so the bar shows how the work itself was split.
tip.load_idle: idle — Exclusive time this node spent with no request at all, sampled every 10 s from its own /admin/api/activity. The second line is its share of the sampled window.
tip.load_lead: Lead — the state that took most of this row's sampled window, with its share.
tip.load_loading: loading — Exclusive time this node spent loading a model. A state of its own: a 453 GB cold load takes about two minutes and is neither idle nor decode.
tip.load_mixed: mixed — Ticks in which the node was prefilling one request while generating another. Kept apart from prefill and decode so nothing is counted twice.
tip.load_no_usage: Without a split — Requests that ended without a usage object (client abort, error, a backend that does not measure). Their tokens may be counted; their prefill and decode time is unknown and is not estimated.
tip.load_prefill: prefill — Exclusive time this node spent prefilling, i.e. with a request between dispatch and its first token. The second line is its share of the sampled window.
tip.load_prefill_s: prefill seconds — Sum of usage.prompt_eval_duration over all answers, measured by oMLX itself and only added up here. Not the client's wait: that is the column beside it.
tip.load_prompt_tokens: prompt tokens — Sum of usage.prompt_tokens over all answers, as the node counted them.
tip.load_remaining: Remaining load time — the node's own estimate, counted down locally; it may be wrong, and the page says when it is.
tip.load_requests: requests — Requests this node answered since the ledger started. Counted by RIPPLE, not by the node; a request that never reached the node is an error and not a request.
tip.load_reset: Reset — Zeroes every counter of this ledger and starts again from now. The file on disk is written before the answer, and the nodes' own count underneath is not touched — it is their number, not ours.
tip.load_seg: Segment — this state's time and its share of the row's sampled window.
tip.load_since: Since — When the window began: the last reset, or the start of the process if the ledger was never reset. The number after the dot is the length of the window.
tip.loaded: loaded — Whether this model's weights are resident on this node. "available" costs disk space only, "loaded" costs memory.
tip.loaded_routable: loaded / routable — Models whose weights are resident on this node (they cost memory), against the models RIPPLE may actually route here — allow-list, policy and offer together.
tip.loading: Load in progress — The node is loading a model; RIPPLE triggered the load and measures it. Size and remaining time come from this node's calibration.
tip.lock: Lock — Whether RIPPLE may take a model's memory away. "closed" means: while the model is loaded, every request that would need exactly this memory is refused (503 model_locked) — on every node that holds it. The lock is not a policy level: the model stays in /v1/models and keeps being served, nothing changes on oMLX. It lives in ~/.ripple/models.yaml and survives a restart of RIPPLE.
tip.maint: Maintenance — A maintenance window declared by the operator: the node accepts no new work, running requests finish. RIPPLE changes nothing on oMLX while doing so — it is routing state. A window with a remaining time ends by itself, a window without an end runs until it is ended.
tip.maint_by: set by — Who set the window: "dashboard" = this button, "operator" = by hand in the file, "calibration" = a calibration run (which is not stored and ends with the run).
tip.maint_done: drained — No request is running on this node any more: the window is empty, the machine can be updated or restarted.
tip.maint_drain: draining — Running requests on a node that accepts no new work. They finish; only at 0 may the machine be touched — a running thread keeps its prefix cache on exactly this node.
tip.maint_left: Remaining — Minutes left in the window, recomputed by the service on every pull. When it runs out the node returns to the pool without further action.
tip.maint_preset: Window length — How long the window applies. "no end" stays until someone ends it — across a restart of RIPPLE as well, because it lives in ~/.ripple/maintenance.yaml.
tip.maint_until: Maintenance until — Moment the window ends by itself, local time of this machine.
tip.max_inflight: max. inflight — Upper bound of concurrent requests; beyond it RIPPLE spills to the other node (FA-5).
tip.max_threads: max. threads — How many thread slots the node may hold.
tip.measured: Measurement age — How long ago the last measurement was taken. A rate from an hour ago says nothing about now.
tip.models_avail: Models available — Models the node offers — not: currently loaded.
tip.node_drain: Drain deadline — How long a removal waits for the requests in flight before it gives up (config.yaml fleet.drain_seconds).
tip.node_id: node_id — The identity the machine reports in /api/cluster/node_id. Slots, affinity and the calibration curve hang off it, so it is read before the node joins.
tip.node_inflight: In flight — The requests RIPPLE has running on this node right now.
tip.node_memory: Memory — used / ceiling as the node reports it in /health (engine_pool): the estimate the guard works with, not the sum of the loaded weights.
tip.node_models: Models — What the node says it carries, read from its model list during the preview.
tip.node_rtt: Round trip — Measured latency of the /health probe that answered, in milliseconds. A property of this moment, not of the machine.
tip.node_scan: From the sweep — What the probe found: the model count, and the measured round trip of the identity probe.
tip.node_site: Site — The location whose networks contain this address (config.yaml sites[].networks). A location, not a routing rule: it never decides where a request goes.
tip.node_source: Source — Whether the node is declared in config.yaml or was added at the page (the runtime overlay).
tip.not_loaded: not loaded — Models the node offers whose weights are not resident — they cost disk space, not memory.
tip.policy: Model policy — Operator state per (node, model), pure RIPPLE state: "disabled" takes the model out of routing here, but it stays in /v1/models as long as another node offers it; "hidden" stops offering it to clients entirely once every node hides it — Hermes and opencode then lose it from their list. Nothing is loaded, unloaded or changed on oMLX; the state lives in ~/.ripple/models.yaml and survives a restart.
tip.policy_orphans: Rules without a table row — Rules from the model file for models this node no longer offers — after an allow-list change, an oMLX update or a deleted model file. The table comes from /healthz and only knows offered models, so such rules would have no row there; here they are listed and can be taken back.
tip.ratio: Occupancy — measured used memory divided by the ceiling.
tip.relative_load: relative load — Share of the node's single-stream rate that is lost right now: 1 − current rate / single-stream rate. 0 % means it still runs at its solo speed; `—` means not measured, not zero.
tip.requests: Requests — Requests RIPPLE has sent to this node since the start.
tip.restart: Restart — Whether this process may end itself at all, what it is waiting for, and how much work is in flight. supervised is launchd's own marker (XPC_SERVICE_NAME); pending means a restart already on its way. The page shows what the service reports and never guesses at it.
tip.restart_delay: Delay — Seconds between the 202 and the exit: the answer has to leave the socket before the process that sends it ends.
tip.restart_inflight: In flight — Requests RIPPLE is serving right now, summed over the fleet, and the nodes that carry them. Above zero a restart needs the second confirmation.
tip.restart_supervised: Supervisor — Whether launchd started this process, and under which job label. Read from the service, never guessed by the page.
tip.rtt: RTT — Measured response time of a probe request to this node; a WAN node would be visible here immediately.
tip.running: running requests — Requests for this model on this node, right now.
tip.samples: Samples — How many completed requests go into the rate; below ten the number is a snapshot.
tip.share_a: Actual share — Actual share of the bound thread slots, right now.
tip.share_t: Target share — Intended share of the thread slots according to the weights.
tip.size_act: Measured size — Memory actually occupied after loading; the difference to the estimate is the calibration error.
tip.size_est: Estimated size — Expected size of the weights from the model configuration, before the node has loaded them.
tip.slots: Thread slots — Bound slots: conversations assigned to this node that keep their prefix cache there.
tip.slots_total: Slots bound — Thread slots this model currently occupies, against the slots its nodes may hold together (max_threads per node).
tip.spill: Spill threshold — From this number of running requests the node counts as full and new work prefers to go elsewhere.
tip.state: State — Result of the last reachability check: does the node answer, does its identity match, does it flap?
tip.taken: Snapshot — Moment of the last pull of /healthz and /stats. The page does not reload, it only replaces the values — the scroll position stays.
tip.target_share: Target share — Share of the thread slots this node should get according to its weight.
tip.th_delete: Delete — drops the thread and frees its slot on this node. The prefix cache cannot be recreated; the next request pays the prefill.
tip.th_idle: idle — Seconds since this thread's last request.
tip.th_key: Key — Client key that opened this thread; no key means the request arrived without one (loopback).
tip.th_remaining: Time left — how long this thread stays bound to this host without a request. At zero the TTL drops it.
tip.th_ttl: TTL — After this time without a request the thread is dropped and frees its slot.
tip.th_turns: Turns — Requests this thread has carried since it was created.
tip.threads_m: Thread slots — Threads of this model that sit on this node.
tip.tps: tok/s — the live per-request decode rate of the model with the most samples on this node, smoothed by the service (alpha 0.3): it falls as requests run in parallel, so it is not a property of the machine. The machine's calibrated capability is not a rate of any model; it stands in the tooltip of the models table, labelled as such.
tip.tps_m: tok/s — the decode rate measured for this model on this node, smoothed by the service (alpha 0.3): it falls as requests run in parallel, so it is not a property of the machine. Measured since this process started; nothing is carried over a restart. A dash means not measured yet; a shown 0.0 is a measurement.
tip.tps_cap: machine capability, not this model: {v} tok/s from the AS-6 calibration in config.yaml — the rate placement.py decides with
tip.used: used memory — Measured model memory of the resident weights on this node — the sum of the actual size after loading, not the estimate from the model configuration, and not the machine's total RAM.
tip.used_est: used memory, estimated — Sum of the estimated model sizes on this node — the value oMLX keeps itself and the guard computes with. It differs from the measurement because the estimate is calibrated.
tip.version: oMLX version — Version the node reports in its own status response.
params.src_page_tip: overrides config.yaml in ~/.ripple/fleet.yaml — the file stays the baseline
params.reset_tip: reset {path} to the value in config.yaml and remove the override
params.weight_confirm: apply weight {w} to new threads only? {n} running threads keep their host until they end
params.edit_tip: Enter saves, Esc cancels — applies to new threads, no restart
params.help.listen: The address and port the proxy binds; it is opened once at start-up, so a change needs an edit here and a restart.
params.help.log_level: How much the process writes to its log (`debug` … `error`); logging is configured before the first request, so a change needs a restart.
params.help.placement.binding_strategy: Which rule picks the host for a new thread: `deficit` follows the weight target, `consistent_hash` a stateless ring, `least_threads` the lowest count — the choice reshapes the whole distribution.
params.help.placement.balance_abs_thresh: The absolute half of the balance hysteresis: the fleet counts as imbalanced only when the weighted load spread exceeds this and the ratio also exceeds `balance_rel_threshold`; in this version the check is computed but gates no placement.
params.help.placement.balance_rel_thresh: The relative half of the balance hysteresis, read as the ratio between the most and least loaded host (1.5 matches the 3:2 target); like the absolute half it only feeds `placement.imbalance()` and moves nothing.
params.help.placement.rebind.enabled: Switches moving a bound thread to another host: while on, an idle thread may move when the decode gain it buys beats the prefill it costs, and while off every thread stays where it was first bound.
params.help.placement.rebind.max_per_hou: The fleet-wide budget of thread moves per hour; once it is spent no thread moves until the hour rolls on, and 0 removes the cap.
params.help.placement.rebind.safety_fact: How much larger the decode gain must be than the prefill cost before a move pays (`gain ≥ cost × factor`); raising it makes moves rarer, lowering it lets marginal moves through.
params.help.placement.rebind.per_thread_: How long one thread is left alone after it was moved; inside that window the sweep never prices it again, so a thread cannot be shuttled back and forth.
params.help.placement.thread_decay_secon: Over how many seconds an idle thread's weight in the deficit falls quadratically to zero; a shorter value frees the fleet from a silent conversation sooner, a longer one keeps its host looking loaded.
params.help.placement.flap_guard_failure: How many consecutive soft probe failures a host may collect before it leaves the pool; 1 drops it on the first failure, and a hard failure (refused connection, identity mismatch) still drops it at once.
params.help.affinity.header: The request header that carries the session id and names a thread exactly; every live thread is recognised through it, so changing the name would orphan all of them and needs a restart.
params.help.affinity.ttl_seconds: How long a thread keeps its slot without a request; after that it is forgotten and the next turn is placed as a new thread.
params.help.affinity.batch_ttl_seconds: The shorter TTL for threads opened by a key of kind `batch`: a job's turns come back to back and nobody waits, so its slot is freed sooner than a conversation's.
params.help.affinity.min_prompt_tokens: Prompts with a single user message below this many tokens are placed by deficit and release their slot as soon as the response returns, instead of holding a thread slot.
params.help.affinity.match_threshold: How similar the stored prefix must be (common characters over request length) for a request to count as the known thread; a lower value keeps an affinity alive across a compression, a higher one splits threads sooner.
params.help.affinity.ephemeral_window_se: How long a finished one-shot request still counts as load on its host, so a burst of short calls is not immediately forgotten by the deficit.
params.help.discovery.interval_seconds: How often every host is probed for health and its model list; a shorter interval notices a change sooner and costs more requests.
params.help.discovery.unhealthy_after: Legacy threshold with no effect: `placement.flap_guard_failures` decides when a host leaves the pool, and a value other than 3 only raises a warning at start-up.
params.help.proxy.retry_other_node: Whether a request that fails before the first byte is tried once on another host; off means the client sees the upstream error instead of a second attempt.
params.help.proxy.request_log: The switch for the one-line-per-request access log (no prompt content, no keys); nothing in the proxy reads it today, so changing it alters no output.
params.help.proxy.connect_timeout_second: The connect timeout towards a host (also used for write and pool); a shorter value hands a dead node to the retry sooner, a longer one waits for a slow machine.
params.help.hosts.*.weight: The host's share of new threads relative to the others, and the divisor of its normalised load; raising it sends more conversations here.
params.help.hosts.*.max_inflight: The hard cap on concurrent requests this host may carry; at the cap it takes nothing more and the request spills to another node or waits.
params.help.hosts.*.spill_threshold: From this many running requests the host counts as full for new threads, even while it still has free slots; it must not exceed `max_inflight`.
params.help.hosts.*.hard_threshold: The fraction of the memory ceiling the cold-load guard admits against; a load that would exceed it evicts models in LRU order until the estimate fits, and a value above 1.0 is refused.
params.help.hosts.*.prefer_resident: Whether an already loaded model makes this host a preferred candidate; off keeps the host in play but lets the deficit decide, so warmth alone no longer attracts work.
params.help.hosts.*.models: The allow-list of models this host may serve; empty means everything it offers, and a model outside the list is never placed here.
params.help.hosts.*.api_key: The credential sent to this host's API; it is read at start-up and shown only as set or none, so a change needs a restart.
update.tip: The newest release on GitHub. ripple update fetches it, runs the test suite and restarts only if the suite is green.
